text:
### Observed differences

- The two windows swap how often two alternative activity blocks run. In the earlier window, A16, A17 and A18 each ran in about 75 in 100 traces, and A19, A20 and A21 each in about 25 in 100; in the later window this is reversed, with A16–A18 at about 25 in 100 and A19–A21 at about 76 in 100. No activity repeats within a trace in either window. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- Routing out of A15 (present in all traces in both windows) shifted accordingly: before, roughly three quarters of A15's outgoing flow went to A16, A17 and A18 (about 27%, 23% and 26%) and one quarter to A19, A20 and A21 (about 14%, 4% and 8%); in the later window about three quarters goes to A19, A20 and A21 (about 25%, 22% and 29%) and one quarter to A16, A17 and A18 (about 9%, 9% and 8%). [DIR001]
- The two blocks are mutually exclusive alternatives in both windows (they never share a trace): before, A16 typically ran without A19 (about 75 in 100), while in the later window A19 typically runs without A16 (about 76 in 100); the same flipped pattern holds for every cross-pair of the two blocks. [REL009, REL010, REL011, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL018, REL019, REL020]
- Relations with A15 and A25 flipped with the blocks: before, A15 was followed by A16/A17/A18 in about 75 in 100 traces with A25 present, and usually ran without A19/A20/A21; in the later window A15 is followed by A19/A20/A21 in about 76 in 100 traces with A25 present, and usually runs without A16/A17/A18. A25 itself runs in essentially every trace in both windows. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL012, REL024]
- The internal structure of each block is unchanged, only its usage flipped: A16/A17/A18 co-occurred in about 75 in 100 traces before (in both orders, no fixed order) and rarely co-occur now (about 25 in 100); A19/A20/A21 rarely co-occurred before (about 25 in 100) and now co-occur in about 76 in 100, again in both orders. [REL007, REL008, REL013, REL022, REL023, REL025]
- A minor positional difference: when A15 and A20 occur in the same trace, their distance in event positions shortened — before it was most often 3 steps (about 52 in 100), in the later window 1–2 steps are most common (about 66 in 100 combined). [LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a change in how often two existing alternative paths after A15 are taken: in the earlier window about three in four cases ran the block A16, A17, A18 after A15 (with A25 alongside), and about one in four ran A19, A20, A21; in the later window these shares reversed to about one in four and three in four. [OCC001, OCC004, DIR001, REL004, REL009, REL012, REL024]

Supporting signs: the participation flip is directly mirrored by the redistribution of A15's outgoing transitions and by the co-occurrence relations of A15 and A25 with each block; every activity involved and both paths are observed in substantial shares in both windows (roughly 25–75 in 100), only the shares between the alternatives shift, while the structure (A15 first, mixed order inside each block, A25 alongside, single execution per trace) stays the same. The volume of qualifying evidence (35 control-flow items against roughly 0.5 expected if nothing had changed) makes chance sampling implausible as an explanation of the ensemble, though many items describe the same underlying trace behaviour and are not independent confirmations. [DIR001, REL001, REL004, REL007, REL022, REL012, OCC001, OCC004]

Limitations: the evidence cannot distinguish a changed routing decision at A15 from a changed mix of cases entering this part of the process (for example a different case population); it shows which path is taken more often, not why. With 200 traces per window the exact shares carry sampling uncertainty, although the size of the flip far exceeds typical sampling variation. [DIR001, OCC001]

Other differences: the positional distance between A15 and A20, measured over traces where both occur, became shorter in the later window (most often 1–2 event positions instead of 3); this is a positional observation and does not by itself show that A20 was moved. [LAG001]
